A lot of accounts are calling a top after this week. Here's why it isn't one, and how you'll know when it's real.

A top isn't a price. It isn't a valuation multiple. It isn't a feeling. A top is a structural condition, and it only confirms after the fact. What you can track in real time is whether the conditions are stacking.

We monitor five:

1. THE FLOOR NARROWS

The cushion between price and the GEX flip is the market's structural insurance. When it shrinks to 3%, then 2%, then 1%, and stays there, the insurance is gone.

2. THE FUEL RUNS OUT

The dealer engine runs on put decay. When institutions stop buying puts, the decay dries up and so does the mechanical bid. The engine doesn't break. It starves.

3. CORRELATIONS SPIKE

When everything becomes one trade, one catalyst unwinds everything. Average pairwise correlation below 0.40 is healthy dispersion. Above 0.55 is herding. Above 0.70 is liquidation.

4. THE REBUILDS FAIL

Every selloff this cycle, the structure rebuilt within 1 to 3 sessions. When the structure breaks and the rebuild doesn't come, the character of the market has changed.

5. THE MAGNETS DISAPPEAR

When cliffs outnumber magnets above price, the structural pull flips from up to down.

HOW THEY STACK:

One is a warning. Two is a watch. Three or more, held together, is the regime change.

Held is the word that matters.

WHERE WE ARE:

Wednesday to Friday, SPY gave back the week. Positive gamma above price fell from about $960M to $295M. The dealer engine went from +39M to -11M. The floor tightened.

That's what a selloff looks like. It isn't what a top looks like.

Last Friday, OPEX: options surface -$2.46B, puts opening 7 to 1. By Monday morning: -$786M and 73% calls.

In June we read 4 of 5. SPY made a new all-time high in August.

February to March, SPY fell 7.7%. Every condition resolved. Price made new highs.

What hasn't happened:

Correlations: green. The selling is dispersed, not one trade.
Rebuilds: the overnight repair showed up Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Monday morning is the next test.

The two conditions that separate a dip from a top haven't fired.

A REAL TOP looks like this: the floor narrows and stays narrow. The fuel thins and doesn't refill. Correlations spike and stay elevated. The rebuild stops showing up. The magnets disappear and don't come back. All of it, together, and held.

We're not there. We track these every session. When they stack, we'll publish it before the event, with the data, on the record.

We'll know it when the data shows it. So will you.
